messages:
alex: heads up — bringing up mistral-7b-v2 (converted to gguf) for eval. quick smoke: outputs look fine qualitatively but logits show token IDs shifted compared to llama-v2 baseline. e.g., prompt 'The capital of France is' -> llama top token 3002 ('Paris'), mistral-convert top token 3014 (which maps to a completely different word). Anyone seen vocab remap during conversion?

julia: hmm, seen this with qwen->ggml conversions. Usually either vocab file mismatch or tokenizer byte-level mapping. Did you use the model's provided vocab.json or the conversion script's fallback?

alex: used convert_v2.py + default vocab from the repo. commands:
```
python convert_v2.py --in mistral-7b-v2.ckpt --out mistral-7b-v2.gguf --vocab vocab.json
```

ken: could be token id offset (e.g., <pad> inserted). Check first 10 token ids for common words from both tokenizers.

alex: good call. quick dump of token ids for ' Paris' (leading space): mistral-tokenizer -> [25, 1023], llama-tokenizer -> [25, 3002]

priya: oh that looks like same prefix token 25 then different continuation. so token id 1023 vs 3002 — might be vocab ordering changes (merging/unmerging). If IDs differ, model weights expect their own embedding matrix ordering. Did conversion remap embeddings by token string or just copy raw arrays?

sam: conversion script we've used for Mistral before remaps by token string when provided a vocab mapping file. If you omit map, it just copies embeddings index-wise. Check convert log: "aligned_vocab=True" vs False.

alex: log shows aligned_vocab=False.

julia: sounds like root cause. If embeddings not aligned, you'd see semantic shift. Options: 1) re-run conversion with aligned vocab mapping 2) construct a token-map by matching token strings and permute embeddings 3) re-tokenize training data (not feasible).

alex: trying aligned conversion now. also seeing small but consistent perplexity bump after int8 quant (Nbits=8). any tips on quantization profiles that minimize topo drift?

ken: we use per-channel symmetric quant for weights + act-order aware calibration. For Mistral, scale sensitivity concentrated in rotary tables and final LN. Try excluding rotary tables from quant and see.

priya: +1. Also test bf16->fp16->int8 path vs fp16->int8 direct. sometimes cast paths matter.

alex: quick experiment: int8 applied to all except rotary and output projection -> ppl delta reduced from +12% to +2% on devset.

sam: nice. keep rotary unquantized and try clamp range calibration with outlier-aware percentiles (99.5th).

julia: also check KV cache alignment. I've seen shifted token ids break KV indexing; if your kv cache indexing assumes tokenid->position mapping but token ids differ, cache reuse could fetch wrong keys. That shows as repeating nonsense at long context.

alex: saw repeating fragments at >2048 tokens when using converted weights on longcontext tests. killing cache fixes it. dump of cache idxs:
```
kv_index[2049] = 3002 (expected 1023)
```

priya: that again points to emb misalignment. Once you align vocab and permute embeddings, KV should match.

ci-bot: deploy note: experimental-models namespace: mistral-7b-v2-gguf-unaligned created at 2026-03-19T10:22:14Z

alex: thanks — re-running conversion with aligned_vocab=True and doing int8-with-rotary-exclude calibration now. will push smoke results in a bit.

julia: if aligned conversion fails, ping me. I have a script that builds a string->id map and permutes weights safely.

sam: also add evals for end-to-end generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE isn't great here) — do human-snipe on a handful.

alex: noted. will run 500-sample eval and post metrics. :thumbsup:
